transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Walker (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Helion Platform), Amira Khan (Helion ML), Salvatore Russo (Helion VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Final week before pilot cutover; agreed to run full dry-run in staging next weekend.
- Discussed canary thresholds (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, quality regressions).
- Agreed runbook edits: add explicit traffic-shift script and KV-cache warmup step; record smoke-test checklist.
- Action items assigned; Redwood to deliver runbook v2 and rollback scripts.

Topics: cutover timing, canary thresholds, A/B routing split, monitoring dashboards, runbook gating, security handoff

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Ethan: Alright team, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45, 50 minutes, um, so we'll walk through the cutover plan, the canary thresholds, and then the runbook changes that Priya's been working on. I want to make sure we have clear owners.
[00:22] Salvatore: Sounds good. Our execs want a crisp timeline — they're nervous about any downtime — so we, we need the safety gates spelled out.
[00:30] Priya: Totally. Quick note — I uploaded runbook v1 in the shared folder, there's a redlined copy that includes the abort conditions. That said, we've already taken a few of Helion's telemetry samples and there are a couple of weird spikes in tokenization latency, which we should talk about.
[00:47] Carlos: Yeah I saw those, it's mostly during long session replay. We have a long-tail of 90th and 99th that we haven't explained yet; could be garbage collector on the app side or KV miss storms.
[01:05] Amira: And also we noticed some slight quality mismatches on generation for very structured prompts — that may surface in the A/B. We set up delta-bleu-like checks in the eval harness.
[01:20] Ethan: Ok, let's start with timeline. Proposed: dry-run in staging Saturday 06/06, weekday limited canary Monday 06/08 4 hours, then escalate to broader canary Tuesday morning, then full traffic Wednesday evening if gates pass. Any conflicts with that?
[01:38] Salvatore: The weekend dry-run is fine as long as we can rewind with the same data; legal wants a snapshot of logs for audit, so retention config needs to be explicit.
[01:50] Priya: We will add a 'log-snapshot' step into the runbook. We also propose a 3-step canary: 1) 5% traffic for 2 hours, 2) 25% for 3 hours, 3) 100% after final check. Each step gated by SLOs: error rate <0.5%, p95 latency <800ms, model output quality regression <2% on eval set.
[02:12] Carlos: That error rate target seems tight for our worst-case workloads. Can we prioritize latency over cost? Because we currently have a fallback path that runs a smaller quantized model but it's lower quality.
[02:26] Ethan: That's the classic tradeoff — dedicated capacity would smooth latency but costs more. For the pilot, the hybrid approach (hosted primary + dedicated burst) could give safety without full commit. We'll add that as an option in the runbook.
[02:40] Amira: Quick question on KV-cache warmup — if we shift traffic to canary nodes, how are you handling KV prefill to avoid cold starts?
[02:52] Priya: Good call. We recommend a two-step warmup: replay a small synthetic prefix set to build KV and then run a small hitting traffic generator for 10 minutes. I'll add exact curl commands in runbook v2.
[03:05] Salvatore: Also want to be sure about observability: can you show exactly which dashboards and panel we will watch? The execs want a single sheet.
[03:16] Priya: We'll publish a condensed 'decision dashboard' with four panels: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error & token-drop rate, KV cache hit ratio, and quality regression trend from the eval harness. We'll include links to the raw Grafana and the Kibana logs.
[03:32] Ethan: I'll also include a small slack channel webhook for the canary alerts and a role-based escalation list.
[03:38] Carlos: On the security side, we need to confirm SSO and the service principal that'll run the cutover scripts. Also KMS keys for any logs that need to be at-rest encrypted per compliance.
[03:51] Ethan: We support customer-managed KMS and SSO provisioning; Priya, can you confirm the steps to add the Helion service account?
[03:58] Priya: Yep — step by step in sec-docs, but for the runbook I'll add a 'pre-cutover security checklist' with fields for the Helion principal, key ARN, and audit-log retention days.
[04:11] Amira: Are there any vendor lock-in or model-variant fallback concerns? Like if capacity is constrained, does Redwood automatically fall back to an earlier model that we've validated?
[04:22] Ethan: There's a routing policy; we can define fallback to a quantized variant with explicit quality tags. We'll include the fallback mapping in runbook v2 as well.
[04:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:34] Ethan: Sorry?
[04:36] Salvatore: No, carry on.
[04:38] Priya: Back to A/B splits — Helion wanted a traffic-split A/B to measure perceived latency and downstream product metrics. We recommend an A/B bucket of 50/50 for the first two hours, then move to canary increments. But A/B adds complexity to routing and metrics lineage.
[04:56] Carlos: We can do A/B but prefer the canary path for safety; maybe run an A/B on a small subset of endpoints that are less business-critical.
[05:07] Amira: I can identify those 5 endpoints — the internal usage ones — and we'll flag them for A/B.
[05:12] Ethan: Great. Now the runbook specifics — Priya, walk us through the abort conditions you added.
[05:17] Priya: Sure. Abort if any of these happen: sustained error rate >1% for 15 minutes, p99 latency spikes above 2s for more than 10 minutes, model-quality regression >4% on the smoke eval, or any upstream auth failure affecting >10% of calls. Those are conservative; we can tweak.
[05:36] Carlos: The model-quality thresholds need to be tied to specific tests. Which eval set are we using? The customer-provided business-critical prompts or the generic dev set?
[05:45] Amira: We'll use a curated Helion-critical set (12 prompts) for the go/no-go. I uploaded it to the shared eval harness earlier.
[05:54] Priya: Yep we integrated that; runbook v2 references 'Helion-critical-v1' eval and the script to run it post-step.
[06:02] Ethan: Ok. Monitoring alerts — what alert routes do we want? Pager for platform on top-tier, slack for product owners, and email for execs?
[06:11] Salvatore: Exactly — and please make sure the exec emails are just summary digests, not every firing alert.
[06:18] Priya: We'll set alert suppression rules for executive channels and add a 10-min dedup window.
[06:23] Ethan: Anything on network/firewall rules for the private endpoints?
[06:27] Carlos: We'll open the necessary ports to Redwood's canary cluster IPs; need the list.
[06:30] Priya: I'll paste the IP CIDR blocks in runbook v2.
[06:33] Amira: One more thing on telemetry — token-level cost breakdowns are critical; we want to analyze cost delta during canary. Can you ensure the metrics feed has token counts and KV cache hit ratio?
[06:44] Ethan: Yes we emit token-level metrics and per-route cost. We'll add an SLO dashboard tile for cost per 1k tokens too.
[06:50] Salvatore: On rollback, do we have a quick circuit breaker if latency or error rooms spike?
[06:55] Priya: The plan has two rollback mechanisms: automated traffic-shift back to previous pool based on alert rule, and manual cutover script that runs a full re-route. We'll keep both.
[07:06] Carlos: What's the plan for sticky sessions? Some of our clients rely on session affinity to keep a long-lived conversation KV. If we shift traffic, we'll lose affinity unless KV is shared.
[07:18] Priya: Good point — for the pilot we'll enable session stickiness for 24 hours for endpoints that require KV persistence; the canary nodes will join a shared KV cluster, and we prefill with the replay step. There's a small window where you could see degraded results but not total failure.
[07:34] Amira: We should also add a customer-visible message in the UI for a brief degradation window during shift, just to set expectations.
[07:40] Salvatore: Yes, product will craft that.
[07:43] Ethan: Now testing specifics for Saturday dry-run — list of things to test: 1) run smoke eval, 2) run tokenized load replay (10k requests), 3) validate sess-stickiness and KV hit ratio, 4) run log snapshot and confirm KMS encryption.
[07:56] Carlos: For the load replay, are you using the synthetic generator or replaying real anonymized traffic?
[08:02] Priya: We'll do a hybrid: anonymized replay for patterns and synthetic for stress tail cases. We have a replay helper script in the repo.
[08:10] Amira: I will anonymize and send a sample by EOD.
[08:14] Ethan: Great. Pricing note — Salvatore asked for delta pricing between hosted + burst vs dedicated for the initial month. I can provide a short table.
[08:24] Salvatore: Need it by Thursday so finance can sign off.
[08:26] Ethan: Ok I'll send it 6/4.
[08:29] Priya: A small transcript glitch— in runbook we also need to include the 'escalation phone tree' in case primary oncall is unreachable.
[08:38] Carlos: We'll add our oncall rotation to the shared doc.
[08:41] Amira: On the A/B measurement, what product metrics will we capture besides latency and quality? We want to measure conversion lift on a specific funnel step.
[08:52] Ethan: We'll capture event counts for the funnel endpoint and pass them into the analytics job — the A/B bucket ids will be in the request headers for attribution.
[08:59] Salvatore: Make sure privacy-preserving hashing is applied to any PII-sensitive fields before shipping to the analytics plane.
[09:05] Priya: Noted — we'll add a preprocessor step to the analytics pipeline.
[09:10] Ethan: Anything else?
[09:12] Carlos: One more minor: are we keeping request bodies in the logs? Legal prefers redact by default.
[09:18] Priya: We'll keep metadata and hashes, full payloads only stored for 7 days and encrypted with customer KMS. Redaction rules will be in the runbook.
[09:27] Amira: Ok that works.
[09:30] Ethan: Let's recap next steps — Redwood to send runbook v2 with scripts and shopping list (CIDRs, service principal steps, rollback scripts). Helion to confirm the 12 critical endpoints, the eval prompts, and share anonymized replay sample. Schedule dry-run Saturday 06/06 02:00 UTC.
[09:49] Salvatore: Good recap — also please include the executive one-sheet with top-line SLOs for them.
[09:55] Ethan: Will do. Anything else?
[09:58] Carlos: No, thanks everyone.
[10:00] Ethan: Alright meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
